propositions: rebar transition exposes two distinct force flags (--force for start-work gate, --force-close for completion gate) while rebar claim uses a single --force, creating inconsistent CLI spelling across similar escape hatches

The retired --force-close flag must be explicitly rejected by the parser with a CommandError rather than silently skipped by the hand-rolled token loop, ensuring stale callers fail loudly instead of accidentally bypassing gates

A bare --force on a close transition records (no reason given) as the reason to match rebar claim parity; --force=<reason> sets an explicit close-gate bypass reason; --force --reason=X on open→in_progress preserves X as the audit note

The collapse of two force flags into one context-dispatched --force[=<reason>] eliminates the spelling collision without introducing new ambiguity, since valueless --force on close was previously parsed and discarded
